etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English cent, from Old French cent, from Latin centum, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱm̥tóm.

definitions.definition: (money) A subunit of currency equal to one-hundredth of the main unit of currency in many countries. Symbol: ¢.

quote.citation: 2015 November 22, “Pennies”, in Last Week Tonight with John Oliver, season 3, episode 35, John Oliver (actor), via HBO:
quote.text: It's true. 1.7 cents to make 1 cent. That really makes the phrase “you have to spend money to make money” ring painfully true.

quote.citation: 1990, Lou Sullivan, From Female to Male: The Life of Jack Bee Garland, →ISBN, page 10:
quote.text: Every cent aside from his own expenses for the barest kind of living went to his down-and-out buddies.

definitions.definition: (money) A subunit of currency equal to one-hundredth of the euro.
(money) A coin having face value of one cent (in either of the above senses).
(music) A hundredth of a semitone or half step.
(nuclear physics) A unit of reactivity equal to one hundredth of a dollar.
(obsolete, except in per cent and cent percent) Abbreviation of centum. One hundred.

quote.text: And broght with hem many stout cent / Of green lordynges.

quote.citation: 1733, Alexander Pope, Moral Essays, Epistle III to Allen, Lord Bathurst, 372:
quote.text: The demon makes his full descent / In one abundant shower of cent per cent.
